features.note: Two rows, 3 cabinets per side, pitch 0.620/0.620 m (dispersion 0.0 mm), alternating black/white on a warm wood-plank floor under the industrial ceiling. Reads as the Panduit showroom aisle of the reference.

The hero SRV-42U rack (glass door) holds the equipment at integer U: the red/blue PDU pair up the rack, a device upper-left, and the stacked base units (UPS 2.95U, FMPS 0.97U, boxes non-intersecting). Reads through the glass door.
UPS/FMPS height ratio 3.05 vs the spec's 3; ceiling Axis camera 101 mm at y=2.70 m; hero cabinet 2.095 m; figure ~1.7 m. The six independently-gated assets read at one coherent scale.
18 red-dominant + 20 blue-dominant meshes — an A/B redundant feed, not two of one colour, matching reference site-08. Reads clearly through the glass.

The lounge reads as a room: mullioned glass partition, city skyline silhouette, conical amber pendants, bar + stools, green carpet, warm daylight ceiling panel — all present and visible from the aisle view.

mechanical.notes: P6 self-check 5/5 by MEASUREMENT (each against the spec's literal wording, with the number beside it). 0 guard failures running AT BOOT; console clean on the real main.js (captured --page); all criticals visible from the view that must show them; both views frame their subject within its cap; correct pick from both views with the two carried rules holding; negative control 13/13 + the reconstructed PDU pick defect caught 4x. Budget 523/1200 draws (44%), 32156/200000 tris (16.1%), 87 hidden meshes at no draw-call cost. A fabricated defect was avoided by verifying a node NAME: the context check read MISSED on the ceiling panel because the script searched 'ceiling_daylight_0' while the node is 'ceiling_daylight' — the panel was present; the instrument was wrong, and checking the name before concluding kept a non-existent defect out of a P6 report. Process: the pass label was changed BEFORE the suite ran this time (the interaction-ui order correction applied to process, not just code). p6_comparison = reference-match (against references/site-01..08 for the views that match a photo viewpoint).

notes: FINAL gate — inline orchestrator judgment. The scene-aisle asset is COMPLETE, and with it the seven-asset Panduit homelab run. It did what no device pass could: put six independently-gated assets in one scene on a single three.js instance, seated at integer U, at one coherent scale, in a reference-backed corridor — and it surfaced the run's deepest verification lessons precisely because it was the first thing to call more than one asset and to judge a composition rather than a datasheet. The five criticals are met by measurement; the honest open item (aisle length) is declared; the closed-asset finding (UPS fan ring) is logged, not patched, with the scope rule that a scene selects declared options but never edits device geometry. Its guard work is the synthesis of the whole run: guards that RELATE two model parts or state a RESULT property (which cannot go stale), a NEGATIVE CONTROL on every one (a guard never seen fail on its own defect is not known to work), verification that runs AT BOOT and AFTER the edit it covers, and measurement in both directions (correct the counter, not the scene; do not optimize what does not matter). Cleared. The run is complete.
